learning_outcomes.text: Explains the concepts of CAD and CAM, the data flow between them, and their use in CNC turning and milling manufacturing processes.
Creates and edits two and three-dimensional part models using CAD software to suit CAM operations.
Plans and creates appropriate CAM operations for CNC turning operations (face turning, internal/external diameter machining, grooving, drilling, and threading).
Plans and execute s profile, pocket, groove, surface machining, and drilling operations using 2, 2.5, and 3-axis CAM operations for CNC milling.

Determines appropriate cutting tools, cutting parameters, and tool approach-plunge-retreat strategies in turning and milling CAM operations; evaluates the machinability of the created tool paths on CNC machines by verifying them with simulation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to CAD/CAM concepts, structure of CAD/CAM systems and their place in the CNC manufacturing process
Creating 2D and 3D drawings using CAD programs for CAM operations
Preparing CAD models for turning operations, introduction to tool path logic and CAM interface
Turning operations: Face turning, external diameter turning and profile machining
Turning operations: Grooving, drilling, internal and external threading
Tool selection for turning, creation of tool position information, determination of cutting parameters and creation of NC codes
3D modeling techniques for milling (Extrude, Revolve, Extrude Cut, etc.)
Editing operations in 3D models (Copy, Array, Chamfer, Fillet, etc.)
Preparation of 2 and 2.5 axis milling CAM operations
Tool selection for milling, creation of tool library and definition of tool offsets
Determination of cutting parameters, tool approach, dive and retraction strategies
Profile machining, grooving, pocketing, surface machining for prismatic parts Machining and drilling operations
Advanced milling applications, 3-axis CAM operations and tool path optimization
Machining of parts on CNC machines with CAM operations, integrated CAD/CAM applications.
